blocks.h2: Water Treatment Options for Evanston Homes

tiles.body: Less scale on fixtures and in heaters.
Very clean water from a dedicated faucet.

bodies: We test hardness, chlorine and sediment at your tap and explain the results plainly.

Evanston treats its own Lake Michigan water, and the city publishes a yearly water quality report. The pipes inside your home are a separate question. For health-related testing, a state-certified lab can run a full panel, and we'll point you to one.

blocks.intro: Evanston runs its own water plant on Lake Michigan and also supplies Skokie and other communities.

items.body: The city reports about 7.8 grains per gallon, which counts as hard. That's enough to leave scale in heaters, on fixtures and in dishwashers.
Many homes are fine without one. Tankless heater owners often benefit most.
In homes with old galvanized pipe, a filter can help with taste and color.

blocks.h2: What Affects the Price of a Softener or Filter
blocks.body: Point-of-use filters are the simplest. Softeners and whole-house filters go on the main line and need a drain and power nearby. The size of the household and the hardness of the water decide how big the equipment needs to be. We test first and quote a flat price.

blocks.h2: Water Treatment Questions From Evanston Homeowners

items.answer: Yes. The city reports about 134 mg/L, or about 7.8 grains per gallon. That counts as hard water.

items.q: Do I need a water softener in Evanston?
items.answer: Not always. If scale is bothering you or you have a tankless heater, a softener can help. We'll test first.

items.q: Softener or filter, what's the difference?
items.preview: Softeners remove minerals. Filters remove other things.
items.answer: A softener removes hardness minerals. A filter removes things like chlorine taste and sediment. Some homes use both.

items.q: How often do filters need changing?
items.answer: Under-sink cartridges every several months. Whole-house filters vary.

items.preview: Check the city's water quality report.
items.answer: The City of Evanston publishes its water quality report each year. It lists what's in the water.

items.q: Can a softener and filter share one install?
items.answer: Yes. We often install them together on the main line.

items.q: How much does water treatment cost in Evanston?
items.preview: It depends on the system. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on the system and installation. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we install.
